Commentary: 14:22 Local Time, 01:22 GMT, 06:52 IST: NZ end with 356. Akash Deep not denied a fifer. India will not be chuffed with their performance today. They would feel at least 50 runs too many. The wicket might not have the same bite like it did yesterday but there is still enough to play with for the seamers. India were shoddy with their fielding and that has costed them further. Three proper chances off Henry went down and even a few close run-out chances were not converted. And India will have more reasons to worry as Bumrah remained wicketless. He looked jaded as well and didn't hit the full tilt that we are so used to. But NZ have the advantage and will look to have a good phase with the ball in the middle session. Indian openers will have the onus again to survive the new ball and lay a platform the rest of the batting order. Henry and co. are itching to go out...

26 overs is the joint-most bowled by Jasprit Bumrah without bagging a single wicket in a Test innings. He had returned 0/57 against the same opponent in the WTC 2021 final in Southampton and 0/79 against England at Lord’s in 2021 - both in 26 overs.

18:30 Local Time, 05:30 GMT, 11:00 IST | Stumps, day 2: It was even-steven at the end of yesterday's play. However, at the end of the second day, New Zealand are firmly on top. India managed to remove Glenn Phillips in the very second over of the day but couldn't run through the tail. Smith, Jamieson and Matt Henry chipped in with crucial lower-order runs while batting alongside Blundell. Akash Deep was once again India's best bowler, claiming his second five-wicket haul in Test cricket, despite three catches being dropped off his bowling. Dropped catches, a few missed run-out opportunities and edges falling short of the fielders meant India conceded at least 50 extra runs. Blundell top-scored with 89 and New Zealand posted 356.

After spending 116.3 overs on the field, India got off to a disastrous start with the bat. Jaiswal left alone the first five deliveries, which were outside off, from Matt Henry before getting castled for a duck. DDP came out with positive intent but played an expansive shot and nicked off for 20. Captain Gill played three lovely off-drives before being undone by a beautiful away-going delivery from Jamieson just before the tea break. Just when a partnership between Rahul and Pant was beginning to look promising, the New Zealand pacer (Duffy) who had a forgettable Wellington Test struck with two crucial breakthroughs. Pant departed while attempting an audacious shot after dancing down the track. KL, meanwhile, smashed a wide delivery straight to backward point. Jurel and Washington batted defensively, doing their best to reach stumps without any further setbacks. Jurel got a reprieve in the penultimate over, but Smith had Washington caught at second slip off the final ball of the day.
116/6 - India trail by 240. The most India have added after the fall of the sixth wicket in a Test innings in New Zealand is 219 (263/6 to 482 all-out) at Auckland in 1990.

India have their backs against the wall at 116/6, still trailing by 240 runs. All the New Zealand pacers have chipped in with wickets and will be eyeing a healthy first-innings lead. Tune in tomorrow to find out how the action unfolds!
